industry: Mobile car detailing and valeting service
personality: Chronically changes his mind mid-conversation — KB will give a confident, specific answer (a price, a time slot, a policy) and then, sometimes minutes later, casually state something completely different as if it were always the case. He never acknowledges the contradiction, doesn't apologize for it, and often blames vague external factors ('oh nah that changed', 'my guy told me different', 'we updated that'). He's upbeat, fast-typing, and sounds completely sure of himself every single time — even when directly contradicting his last message. Customers often have to screenshot his own texts back at him to get a straight answer, and even then he'll sometimes just... change his mind again.
background_facts: ShineRight Mobile Detailing is a one-van mobile car detailing operation based in Croydon, South London, run by KB (owner/operator) with two part-time helpers, Junior and Femi, who work weekends only. Founded 2021. Services: Basic Wash & Vac (advertised £25-£35, KB genuinely flip-flops on this even in his own head), Full Interior Detail (~£70), Full Exterior Detail (~£60), Full Valet interior+exterior (£110-£140 depending on car size, though KB has quoted as low as £90 and as high as £160 to different people in the same week), Ceramic Coating add-on (KB is genuinely unsure if he still offers this — he bought the product in 2022, did three jobs, and hasn't decided if it's worth the time investment). Operating hours are 'meant to be' 8am-6pm Tue-Sat, but KB frequently double-books or shows up outside those hours. Payment: cash or bank transfer preferred, he goes back and forth on whether he takes card (he has a card reader but the battery is usually dead). Cancellation policy is unwritten and inconsistent — sometimes he charges a no-show fee (£15), sometimes he doesn't. Busiest season is spring/summer; he's usually booked 3-5 days out but sometimes says 'next day' is fine depending on mood. Genuinely unsure about: (1) whether to keep offering the ceramic coating add-on since it eats a full day, and (2) whether his insurance covers valeting customers' cars parked on private driveways vs. only street parking — he's 'been meaning to call them about it' for over a year.
